As for the question I sometimes go to sleep with my makeup on, but only if it's just mascara and blush. Although if I don't feel like taking off my makeup I imagine myself waking up with a lot of zits so that helps me to just doing it.

omg I am always picking... me...my so... my dogs (they get pimples too).... shity nephew and I bond over arm pimples or what not. haven't solved it yet. I did stop buying my nails for a bit. not I mostly cut them vs chew.
I don't know what it is with arm pimples but I suddenly got a ton of them a few months ago. I think if you scratch one of them open you are doom to bumps everywhere :S

I overcame the majority of the picking issues when I started wearing makeup (having foundation on during the day just makes me not want to touch my face & fuck things up). Getting a good skincare routine came about when I discovered Korean skincare. The thought of washing my face every night before bed always just seemed like a chore, and moisturizer pffft... Now as odd as it seems, I look forward to 8 or 9 various steps in my night routine to remove makeup & pamper my face, it's totally relaxing and my skin is so much better. Makeup is now a fun accessory instead of mainly a way to cover up of bad skin. I do still have a problem with washing my brushes too infrequently, I don't know how to break that bad habit. If anyone has any tips I'd love to know!

I love AB so much. I go in and out of using the full routine. Right now it's just the su:m 37 rose stick and ceravae since I haven't been home in a couple months and am on the road. Ah, brushes. I think I have washed my brushes about twice. I skirt around them by using the same eyeshadows just to avoid cleaning them.

My bad habit was washing my makeup brushes once a month or so, and I now wash them on a weekly basis. I didn't break that bad habit intentionally, it was more that I bought a beauty blender, and I wash that after every other use. Washing that SO often makes me feel like it's been way longer since I last washed my makeup brushes, so now I wash them approximately once a week.
That's good! I know the blender is a bit of an investment, so it's good it fostered a good habit! I bought a knock off and it wasn't long before it got moldy.

My worst pattern is not washing my brushes, so to try and encourage myself to do it I make it as easy as humanly possible. I'll buy the spray-in cleaner, or the brush wipes, and use those when I feel really lazy, and then give them a good washing at least once a month. It helps, even if it isn't great. I also bought makeup removal wipes for my face to start to encourage myself not to sleep in my makeup, and was able to eventually transition into a decent skincare routine!
